pairs.subject: game-economy-tuning
pairs.evidence: src/lib/catalog/pipelines/currencies.ts:207 The currency balance step derives ~58,400 G/hr faucet vs ~42,900 G/hr sink in its own comment (outside ±15%), then ships hand-typed 'relative units' 110/105 that the ±15% checker passes, which is exactly the placeholder-manufactures-a-pass failure the band technique forbids.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/catalog/pipelines/currencies.ts:207 Comment at line 202 derives a 42,900 G/hr sink ('scaled down to match typical active playstyle'); the checker receives 110/105 instead of the derived rates, so the band is never pointed at the stated economy.

src/lib/catalog/pipelines/currencies.ts:115 Orb drains carry no throughput estimate and are declared self-balancing (line 221) rather than recorded as unestimated; item sell-back (an item→gold converter) is filed as a plain faucet.

src/lib/catalog/pipelines/progression-curves.ts:180 The family is stated as geometric (line 22), but acceptance only checks the exponent coefficient against ±10%. It never evaluates the curve over its range or computes the step-ratio CV, so a polynomial formula carrying exponent 1.08 would pass.
src/lib/catalog/pipelines/items.ts:697 Each item's price is derived against a power score in one central unit and audited by priceRatioWithinBand (items.ts:733) against the 0.8–1.2× curve.

pairs.subject: game-economy-tuning
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_progression/_internals/XpTableGenerator/helpers.ts:103 The XP table generator exports a polynomial curve (base × L^exp, via calculateXpForLevel) into a UE DataTable and loader, while the project canon (progression-curves pipeline) states a geometric family (base × 1.08^L). There is no family diagnostic and no recorded exception, so a shape error ships as tuning.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_progression/_internals/XpTableGenerator/helpers.ts:26 calculateXpForLevel is Math.floor(base * Math.pow(level, exponent)), which is polynomial, against the canon's geometric claim. No step-ratio CV check runs over the 1..MAX_LEVEL range.

pairs.subject: game-economy-tuning
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/metrics/lootMetricsView.ts:101 The loot dashboard's read model prints the affix pool size, a tier count and a pity dry streak. It never computes the five decay measurables (top-rarity share >15%, single modifier >20% of pool, drop rate vs baseline 3x/5x, power gain <2%/level, upgrades <0.5/level), so the flattening of a loot economy cannot show up.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/metrics/lootMetricsView.ts:101 The affix glyph reports pool size, not the share of the most common modifier. The weights glyph (line 97) reports a tier count with shares only in a tooltip, with no 15% threshold. The drought reading is a p95 legendary dry streak in kills, not upgrades per level.
